newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower, weather weakens Sept.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower, weather weakens Sept.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended lower, with September under pressure after warm, dry weather allowed planting to advance over the weekend in the northern U.S. Plains, traders said.
Mill-related buying helped restrict losses in front-month July spring wheat, traders said.
Traders said commercial support in the July contract helped the July/September spread widen by three cents to close at 7-3/4 cents per bushel.
MGE spring wheat settled 1/4 to four cents lower, with July down 1/4 cent at $3.90-1/2.
September lost 3-1/4 cents to close at $3.82-3/4.
Traders said Cargill was the featured player, buying at least one million July bushels. ADM and General Mills also each bought a few hundred thousand July bushels.
Featured sellers included Benson-Quinn, which sold 800,000 July. Of that, 350,000 bushels were sold at the session's close, traders said.
